chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Mansur ibn Kharaja, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the Zakat al-Fitr. He said: 'A sa' of dates, or half a sa' of wheat, or a sa' of barley, and dates are more beloved to me.'

key_terms.صَاعٌ: A sa' (a traditional unit of volume measurement)
key_terms.صَدَقَةُ الْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitr (alms of breaking the fast)

ai.seo_question: What are the valid food items and quantities for Zakat al-Fitr according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the canonical measures for Zakat al-Fitr, prioritizing dates as the preferred medium, a stance that reflects the agricultural and economic context of Medina. It underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the intrinsic value of the food item itself rather than its monetary equivalent, distinguishing it from later practices of paying cash. The preference for dates highlights their status as a staple sustenance and a symbol of generosity during the festive occasion of Eid.
